overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated shorts reveals a massive performance bifurcation: second-person immersive survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') focusing on lethal cosmic environments dominate views and engagement (800–1,000+ views, 3.5%+ like rates), whereas psychology and generic biological trivia ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', earworms, octopus hearts) consistently stall below 100 views. Recent uploads confirm audience preference for visceral, high-stakes extreme physics and planetary anomalies.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Planetary Hazard ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) yield the channel's highest engagement rates.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize the immersive 'What If You Fell / Stepped Into...' framing for cosmic and environmental physics shorts.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,029 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) drove top-tier views within recent windows.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on counter-intuitive scientific facts with concrete visual imagery (e.g., vaporized rock, magnetic dissolution, crushing tides).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded multiple times garnered 5–53 views and 0 likes; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' capped at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic brain facts and psychology lifehacks until narrative micro-drama or visual storytelling frameworks can be integrated.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple re-posts of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' flatlined at low engagement relative to frequency.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content from dry biology flashcards to intense cinematic survival encounters.

next_video.opening_direction: Start instantly with high-speed zoom into a pulsing, hyper-dense neutron star with the audio hook: 'If you got within 1,000 kilometers of this dead star, you wouldn't crash—your body would dissolve at the atomic level.'
next_video.twist_direction: Explain that the magnetic field is a quadrillion times stronger than Earth's, pulling the iron straight out of your hemoglobin and stretching your atoms into needle-thin cylinders before you even feel heat.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'What If / Fatal Hazard' hook and high-stakes space mystery that generated peak viewership on the channel, while introducing an untouched entity (Magnetars) away from overdone exoplanet rain tropes.

experiment: Test a 21-second 'cinematic body-horror space physics' narrative pacing with zero intro padding, measuring whether extreme physics consequences retain viewer completion past the 15-second mark compared to exoplanet descriptions.
